topic.subject: science
topic.title: Electric circuits
topic.scope: cell, bulb, switch, closed and open circuits, conductors and insulators, series connection of cells

misconceptions.statement: A battery is a source of electricity that gets used up and disappears.
misconceptions.why: Students observe that batteries stop working after some time and assume the physical substance inside is consumed or lost.
misconceptions.fix: A cell converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy; it does not disappear but runs out of chemical potential.

probe.question: Where does the electricity go when a battery dies?
probe.wrong_answer: It is all used up and has vanished into the air.

misconceptions.statement: Electricity flows from the battery to the bulb, but not back to the battery.
misconceptions.why: Students often view the battery as a 'source' that pushes energy out, similar to how a tap pushes water out.
misconceptions.fix: Electricity requires a continuous, unbroken path (a closed loop) from one terminal of the cell, through the bulb, and back to the other terminal.

probe.question: Why do we need two wires connected to the bulb?
probe.wrong_answer: One wire is enough to carry the electricity to the bulb to make it glow.

misconceptions.statement: The switch consumes electricity to turn the light on.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the function of a switch as a 'power' device rather than a simple mechanism to break or complete a path.
misconceptions.fix: A switch does not consume electricity; it simply acts as a bridge that connects or disconnects the path for current to flow.

probe.question: What happens to the electricity when you turn the switch off?
probe.wrong_answer: The switch absorbs the electricity so it doesn't reach the bulb.

misconceptions.why: Textbooks often use metal wires as the primary example, leading students to overgeneralize.
misconceptions.fix: While most metals are good conductors, other materials like graphite or salty water can also conduct electricity.

probe.question: Can a pencil lead (graphite) conduct electricity in a circuit?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it is not a metal.
